official.deadline_note: Two fixed submission dates are published for the university scholarship funds, Kranken- und Unfallfonds, Legat Grobe and the Lichtenstein Foundation: until June 15 for the fall semester and until January 15 for the spring semester. 15 January 2027 (spring semester) is the next upcoming date as of the verification date; the fall-semester date falls on 15 June 2027. Cantonal education contributions (Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft) are decided and scheduled by the cantonal offices, whose institutional deadlines differ.
official.application_cycle: Semester cycle: fall-semester applications until June 15, spring-semester applications until January 15
official.status_note: The Submission Deadlines page publishes the standing semester submission dates (until June 15 for the fall semester, until January 15 for the spring semester) for the university scholarship funds, Kranken- und Unfallfonds, Legat Grobe and the Lichtenstein Foundation, and no closure of the current round is announced.

official.duration: Awards are organized per semester (fall/spring submission rounds); the university scholarship funds and Legat Grobe pay per month, the Solifonds per semester
official.description: The University of Basel has its own fund to aid students with very limited resources and from low-income families, awarding partial scholarships primarily during the final degree phase (BA/MA). Scholarships from the university are granted by the scholarship committee of the Senate in addition to any cantonal education contributions, and the student welfare office advises students and assists with applications.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you can win from abroad: it is need-based top-up money for students already enrolled at Basel, paid mainly in the closing BA/MA phase at CHF 200-600 per month, and it sits on top of cantonal education grants rather than replacing them. The realistic route is to secure cantonal funding from Basel-Stadt or Basel-Landschaft first, then approach the student welfare office (sozialberatung@unibas.ch, +41 61 207 30 38) well before the June 15 or January 15 cut-off. International applicants are explicitly pointed toward home-country scholarships, so do not build a Basel budget around these funds. Enrolled students with very limited resources should still reach out: the office states it helps with the submission itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled Basel students in the final phase of a BA/MA who have very limited resources and already hold, or can obtain, cantonal education contributions.
application_readiness_checklist: Get enrolled at the University of Basel first - the university funds are for enrolled students, not applicants

Check your eligibility for cantonal education contributions (Basel-Stadt: Amt für Ausbildungsbeiträge; Basel-Landschaft; or ausbildungsbeitraege.ch for all cantons) before applying, since university awards are explicitly supplementary
Email or call the Social Services office (sozialberatung@unibas.ch, +41 61 207 30 38) to discuss your case and confirm which fund fits your situation
Diarize the cut-off: until 15 June for the fall semester, until 15 January for the spring semester
For illness or accident costs, apply before treatment wherever possible and prepare a cost estimate
common_rejection_risks: Applying before enrolment at the University of Basel - the funds target enrolled students
Applying outside the final degree phase (BA/MA), which is where the university scholarship funds are primarily awarded
Presenting the university award as primary funding instead of a supplement to cantonal education contributions
Missing the hard 15 June / 15 January submission dates, which apply even to the specific named funds
International applicants assuming eligibility, when the official page redirects them to home-country scholarships
Applying for Legat Grobe or the Lichtenstein Foundation without meeting the subject or citizenship conditions
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The awards are partial and supplementary: expect to fund rent, food, health insurance and study materials yourself from cantonal contributions, family support or work. Basel is one of Switzerland's most expensive student cities, so a monthly top-up of CHF 200-600 (or CHF 500-1000 per semester from the Solifonds) will cover only a slice of living costs, and the university pages publish no figure for what else is covered.
document_audit: No document list is published for the scholarship funds, so confirm the exact dossier directly with the student welfare office rather than assuming a standard form exists
The only published document requirement is a cost estimate for the Health and Accident Fund, submitted if possible before treatment
Keep your cantonal education contribution decision and amount on hand, since university awards are assessed against that base
The office explicitly offers help with the submission, so an incomplete first approach is low-risk - but only if you start before the deadline
alerts: The submission deadlines carry an asterisk on the official page whose footnote is not rendered in the page text - treat 15 June / 15 January as strict and verify the fine print with the student welfare office
University scholarship funds are primarily for the final degree phase (BA/MA) only
The Margarete and Walter Lichtenstein Foundation requires Swiss citizenship
Legat Grobe is limited to biology students with a zoology/botany focal area
Cantonal offices in Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft run their own deadlines, which differ from the university's
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Direct application to the Social Services student welfare office (Petersplatz 1, Basel), which advises on the funds, helps assemble the submission and administers awards on a semester cycle keyed to the 15 June and 15 January dates.
